the subjective qualities of material perception are distinct and systematic, and that they can be used to classify materials into different classes.
the perceptual qualities of materials are well defined, and that they are systematically related to material membership.
the visual and semantic judgments of material properties are consistent and that the material classes are well clustered in the space of material properties.

the question: How do we perceive and understand the world around us?

the nature of the perceptual qualities of material appearance and how they interact with material classes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that perceptual properties of materials are not only important in the context of materials classification, but also have a significant role in the perception of materials.
material classification and material quality judgments share common information and are highly related to each other, and thus they are likely to facilitate each other.
material classes are perceptually well-defined, distinct, and consistently related to material qualities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

material properties are not just a collection of independent features, but instead are organized into a small number of perceptual dimensions, and that these dimensions have a natural correspondence with material classes.
the human visual system has a strong ability to group materials into classes, and to judge their perceptual properties.
there is a small set of perceptual features that capture the essence of material perception.
